    A Second Life for Clothes

    SECOND LIFELIFE for

    What happens to the clothes we no longer wear?

    One person's unwanted clothes can become another person's opportunity.

    The Clothes we leave behind

    02 — The collage Every wardrobe has them: a jacket that no longer fits, jeans that are out of style, children's clothes that are suddenly too small. We put them in a bag and forget about them. But a bag of old clothes does not simply disappear. Tap the objects to see what happens to them.

    A Second Life for Clothes— 02 —
    The founders · LikeKomek
    03 — How it all started

    The Beginning

    The story began at home, with a simple decision to declutter. Asemgul Kereibayeva, one of the two founders, collected her own clothes and her children's clothes. The children had grown, and the things no longer fit them.

    She looked for a place in Astana where she could donate them and found a charity foundation. When she brought the bags there, she was shocked: it turned out that a lot of people in Astana were in need.

    For us, it is just clothing. For someone else, it can be worth its weight in gold.

    — Asemgul Kereibayeva, co-founder of LikeKomek

    At home, she told her husband, Daulet Kereibayev, that she wanted to start a project to help people. He supported her, but he also started thinking about the practical side. How would it all work?

    07 — Upcycling

    Denim transformation from old jeans to new design

    Denim is one of the most common things in a donation bag, and it often arrives too worn to wear again. For two years now, LikeKomek has worked with the Kazakh brand Artmate. Denim that is not fit for wearing is collected separately and no longer goes to the rubbish.

    From old jeans, new traditional-style pieces are made: chapans, vests and shalbars, along with many other designs.

    We don't send unwearable denim to the rubbish anymore. We give these things a second life too.— Asemgul Kereibayeva, co-founder of LikeKomek
    08 — The limits

    Not everythingcan be saved

    ⚠ Not reusable Torn
    Dirty Broken
    The honest part

    This is the part of the story that rarely appears in photos. Some donations cannot become anything. Torn or dirty clothes, torn shoes and broken toys end up as rubbish.

    The reason is simple and honest: LikeKomek does not have a full recycling cycle. It can only recycle part of what it receives, through upcycling.

    Unfortunately, all of this goes to the rubbish, because we don't have a full recycling cycle.— Asemgul Kereibayeva, co-founder of LikeKomek

    In a garage near the warehouse, the team keeps everything that will go to the landfill.

    The shoebox problem

    People often donate shoeboxes. The team tries to reuse as many as possible. The rest are pressed, so they take up less space, and then they are sent for recycling.

    According to the figures LikeKomek gave us, 740 kg of cardboard was sent for recycling. See “Impact in numbers”.

    A business with a social purpose

    “Yes, it is a business, but it is a social one,” says Asemgul Kereibayeva. LikeKomek is listed in the register of social entrepreneurs and in the register of the Green Technologies Center, because its work is also connected to ecology.

    The
    Journey     continues
    11 — Final page

    A bag of old clothes looks like the end of a story. At the LikeKomek warehouse, it is the beginning of many. A child's jacket goes to a village. A worn towel keeps a shelter animal warm in winter. A pair of old jeans becomes a chapan. A shirt with a new label finds a buyer for a few hundred tenge.

    But not every journey has a happy ending. Torn shoes, broken toys and dirty clothes still go to the landfill, because there is no full recycling cycle yet.

    Behind the simple idea — “you just take things for free and sell them” — there is a warehouse, a sorting table, vans, salaries and rent. “Before, it wasn't like that,” Asemgul remembers. “We had to spin like a squirrel in a wheel.”

    A second life for clothes starts before the donation: with clean, wearable things, given with the next owner in mind.

    One person's unwanted clothes can become another person's opportunity.
